summary.text: Raul Turrieta is the Democratic candidate for the New Mexico House of Representatives, District 39, in the November 3, 2026 general election.

A Navy veteran and longtime Grant County Assessor's Office employee, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that his priorities include protecting Medicaid, strengthening rural hospitals and cutting taxes for working families.

paragraphs.text: Raul Turrieta graduated from Silver High School and works in public administration.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a lifelong resident of Silver City who grew up in a working-class family; he said his father and grandfather were union members at the Chino Mine.
He said he served in the U.S. Navy aboard the submarine tenders USS Howard W. Gilmore and USS Dixon before beginning work at the Grant County Assessor's Office in 1981.
Turrieta said he was elected Grant County Assessor in 1999, served four terms, and now works as Chief Deputy Assessor.
He also said he has hosted the Local Flavor radio show on KURU for more than a decade, coached youth sports and hosted local nonprofit fundraisers.
He advanced from the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026.

Turrieta said his main goal is affordable, high-quality health care in southwestern New Mexico, including protecting Medicaid, strengthening rural hospitals, lowering prescription drug costs and addressing medical debt.
He also said he would work to cut taxes for working families and ensure that wealthy New Mexicans and large corporations pay their fair share.
